headline: Verizon confirms $10 monthly fee for new iPhone Handoff feature
summary: Verizon joins T-Mobile and Deutsche Telekom in charging for Apple's new iPhone Handoff. This feature allows users to seamlessly switch their phone number between multiple iPhones.
details: Verizon has confirmed a $10 monthly fee for Apple's new iPhone Handoff feature. This follows similar charges announced by T-Mobile and Deutsche Telekom for the same service.
The iPhone Handoff feature allows users to seamlessly switch their primary phone number between multiple iPhones. This enables a single number to be active on different devices at different times.

While the feature offers convenience for users with multiple Apple devices, the additional monthly charge from carriers adds to the cost of ownership. This pricing strategy by major carriers could influence adoption rates.

headline_marked: [[Tesla driver asleep using FSD crashes]] into highway patrol cars, injuring two officers
headline: Tesla driver asleep using FSD crashes into highway patrol cars, injuring two officers
summary: A Tesla driver claims he was asleep while using Full Self-Driving when his car collided with two CHP vehicles, seriously injuring two officers. This incident reignites concerns over driver-assist system safety.
details: A Tesla driver claims he was asleep and using the Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature when his vehicle crashed into two California Highway Patrol (CHP) cars. The incident, captured on video, seriously injured two CHP officers who were responding to an earlier accident on I-80.

CHP officials issued a warning, emphasizing that "Despite its name, full self-driving is not fully autonomous." They stressed that technology does not absolve drivers of their responsibility to safely operate their vehicles.

Following numerous collisions involving parked emergency vehicles, the NHTSA launched an investigation into Tesla’s Autopilot software in 2021. The agency's report found that driver-assist features failed to keep drivers engaged, linking them to hundreds of crashes and dozens of deaths.

Tesla released an Autopilot update in 2023, adding more controls and alerts to ensure drivers maintain control when Autosteer is active. However, the NHTSA subsequently opened another investigation to assess the adequacy of these changes.
